title: Restitution as an independent basis of liability
shortTitle: Restitution as an independent basis of liability
summary: Receipt and retention of a benefit can generate liability for unjust enrichment even without a promise.
notes: The introduction gives mistaken payments, mistakenly performed services, and improvements to another’s property as examples. It distinguishes a mistaken transfer from an unrequested benefit voluntarily imposed by an officious intermeddler. When bargaining is feasible, the text explains why a person cannot ordinarily force someone else to pay for an unsolicited service. Emergency intervention can present a different question. The following Cotnam opinion begins on the last assigned page, so its full reasoning is not available within the assignment.
